newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler shares favoured in downbeat market.
newsitem.headline: Daimler shares favoured in downbeat market.

text.p: Shares in Germany's Daimler-Benz AG rose on Friday against the market trend after announcing a traffic telematics joint venture and following a favourable meeting with analysts Thursday, dealers said.
Daimler shares were up 1.05 marks at 127.50 marks at 1104 GMT, while the DAX index was down 0.5 percent at 3,334.69 points. Turnover in the shares were relatively modest, however.

The company earlier said its Debis unit planned a joint venture with Deutsche Telekom unit T-Mobil to set up a traffic telematics venture that would generate 200 million marks in sales within three years.
Dealers said that news was taken up well in the markets and also said Daimler chief executive Juergen Schrempp's meeting with Goldman Sachs outside Frankfurt on Thursday had gone well.
"Analysts said they were happy with that," said one dealer.
Other car shares were markedly weaker with BMW down 3.5 percent and VW down 3.3 percent.
Dealers noted that these two stocks had been very strong earlier in the week so part of their declines were due to profit-taking.
